arc.title: The Long Round
arc.premise: The first disc ever thrown never landed. It is still riding the wind, and the wind it drags behind it is why nothing on this trail is ever calm. You arrive where it just passed. You always will.
arc.unlock: Pack N+1 requires pack N beaten. Holes unlock sequentially inside a pack, and a pack's back five opens once its front five has been finished once.
arc.beaten: Sum of every half's best <= target, so a ten-hole pack scores nothing until both halves have been finished once. Stars: 1 = finished, 2 = beat target, 3 = beat elite. Beaten packs unlock free replay of any hole.
arc.$comment: The trail has no last stop. `weeks` and `holesPerPack` are legacy cadence machinery kept for decode compatibility and read only by currentWeek, which gates nothing; every count comes from LevelsCatalog.totalHoles/packCount. Packs beyond the authored six are appended and unlock the same way.

packs.$curation: Re-authored 2026-08-03 after the first cut shipped and played easy. Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, farm pinned, brief forced. Gates: the brief's feature present in the built terrain, the hairpin floor raised 0.70 -> 0.80 (farm's dogleg ceiling), finishable by the ideal player in calm air AND under the authored wind, and — new — every hole DEFENDED both ways: trouble past the pin (water, or cover standing in the 2-26m band behind it) and trouble short (water on the approach, or >= 3 blocking props over the last 45m). The bomber is a documented exception: that brief clears its own corridor, so it had 0 guarding props on all 48 candidates every sweep, and is gated on long trouble alone at a higher bar. Certification rates under the defence gate: ridge 8/48, pocket 48/48, bomber 11/48, island 48/48, bend 2/48.
packs.$tuning: The first cut was built on the idea that a tailwind starves the disc of lift and lands it short. It does not — measured through the real model, a 24mph tailwind adds ~15m to a drive (109.7 -> 124.8) and doubles a flop (28.5 -> 57.7). So the pack handed out free distance and the holes had nothing to charge for it, which is exactly how it played. The wind still comes from behind on every hole; what changed is that overshooting now costs. Note what the sweep turned up while gating this: the oval platform puts its rim 30-39m past the pin on EVERY hole this generator makes, so out of bounds never punishes an overthrow — long trouble has to be water or cover. Harness ideal is 13 calm / 12 under the authored wind against a pack par of 10. Star lines are 9 / 7, set BY THE AUTHOR rather than extrapolated: they sit 4 and 6 under the harness ideal, where packs 1 and 2 sit at ideal-1 / ideal-3. That is deliberate and it is the tightest pack in the arc — note two stars is also the gate on pack 4, so if 9 proves out of reach the fix is to loosen it here rather than to grind. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 19 (front 10 + back 9). Star lines design (front five identical).

packs.$curation: Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, reef pinned, brief forced, certified in calm air AND under the authored wind, and DEFENDED both ways. Certification rates: pocket 46/48, ridge 27/48, island 48/48, bend par 1 14/48, bend par 2 18/48. Hole 3 was authored par 2 and re-swept as a par 1: all 48 certified candidates at par 2 were an ideal-player ace, so the par carried no information — the same tell that made pack 2's ridge a par 1 — and the par-1 brief deals a different, harder set of holes (ideal 2). Reef has NO LAKE (BiomeCatalog gives it lake 0.0...0.0, it being a submerged scenery), so the only water a reef hole can carve is an island's own moat; every other hole here is defended by coral, which reef has more of than any other scenery (55-100 props). packs.$tuning: The stub sold this pack as "water everywhere", and reef cannot deal that — see the curation note. The mechanic is the other half of what the stub said, the flop, and the current is a CROSSING one because that is what actually costs here: scripts/sweep-pack's `wind` probe puts the ideal player at 1.90/2.04 across the line against 1.42/1.46 along it, the opposite of the arc's assumption that the headwind is always the punishing direction. These holes are short, so drift beats carry. Pack 2 is nominally the crosswind pack but is asking a different question — aim-off on a long bend, against hang time on a short drop, and a flop is the shot that hangs. Harness ideal is 9 calm / 11 under the authored wind against a pack par of 7. Star lines 8/6 are PROVISIONAL at ideal−1 / ideal−3, same reasoning as pack 4: unplayed content gets the pack 1/2 shape, not pack 3's author-tightened one. packs.$curation: Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack p6): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, volcano pinned, brief forced, certified in calm air AND under the authored wind, and DEFENDED both ways. The finale plays ALL FIVE briefs, one each. Certification rates: bend par 2 13/48, pocket par 2 47/48, ridge par 1 28/48, bomber par 2 4/48, island par 2 48/48. The bomber was authored par 3 and re-swept as a par 2: at par 3 exactly one candidate in 48 certified and the ideal player went round it in 2, the same no-information tell that dropped pack 2's ridge and pack 5's island a rung. Volcano is the hardest scenery in the arc to deal a bomber on (the scout certifies 1-4 of 32 at every par) because that brief clears a corridor and this mountain's defence is what stands in it; the winner is the only one of the four that clears the general defended gate rather than the bomber's raised long-trouble exemption. No gate was softened for this pack: volcano clears pack 3's defended gate on its own props (10-26 blockers guard a typical approach) and pack 3's story-fit floors untouched (dogleg 0.80-0.95, berms 16-19m). The moat and the dealt lake are both LAVA here (the scenery-coherence pass), so 'wet' in these receipts is the mountain's own hazard. Sweep date: 2026-08-05.
packs.$tuning: WINDS ARE CROSSWINDS, and that is a measurement rather than a mood. The design project authored the finale as a dead headwind from 0 degrees — the thing overhead comes low and you throw straight into it — and scripts/sweep-pack's `wind` probe puts the ideal player at 1.58 into a volcano headwind and 1.54 with it, against 2.06 across the line either way. This mountain is reef's shape, not city's. So the bearings march round the compass (224 -> 262 -> 288 -> 66 -> 96) because the thing is circling, and every one of them sits on or near a cross axis because that is where volcano actually charges. That is the third time the arc has assumed a wind direction and been wrong; the probe is cheaper than the re-author. TWO GALES — the bomber set piece and hole 30 itself — are the one deliberate break of the arc's one-gale rule, and this is the pack that gets to break it. Harness ideal is 11 calm / 10 under the authored wind against a pack par of 9. Star lines 11 / 9 are PROVISIONAL at target = calm ideal, elite = ideal-2 — packs 2 and 4's shape for unplayed content, not pack 3's author-tightened one. If the finale proves cruel, loosen target before softening the winds: the winds are the only thing here that was measured. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 19 (front 9 + back 10). Star lines design (front five identical).

packs.title: Into the Teeth
packs.mechanic: Into the wind — every hole is thrown into the face of it, so the disc stops short of the line the arc draws and the answer is a rung up the ladder rather than an aim-off.

packs.$tuning: THE WIND IS A HEADWIND, and that is the pack. Every bearing sits within 20 degrees of 0 — the thing overhead went north and the wind it drags is coming back down the line at you — which makes this the first stop on the trail that tests the loft ladder rather than aim-off. Packs 1 and 2 are crosswind reading and shaping, pack 3 is downwind trouble; into it was the one axis the introduction never asked about. STAR LINES ARE PROVISIONAL AND DELIBERATELY NOT PACK 6's SHAPE. Harness ideal is 22 calm and 25 under the authored wind, against a pack par of 19 — the first pack where the authored wind costs MORE than the calm ideal by a clear margin (+3), which is the mechanic working. Setting target at the calm ideal the way pack 6 did would price the pack as if its own wind were not there, so target follows the WINDY ideal (26 = windy ideal + 1) and elite sits at the calm ideal (22). If it proves cruel, loosen target before touching the winds: the winds are the only thing here that was measured. Every PlaytestHarness number is a floor — it has perfect knowledge of the flight model — so real play is harder than these lines assume, never easier. ONE GALE, on the long hole (10), per the arc's rule; pack 6's two-gale break is not inherited. Ten holes, front five and back five, packPar 19.

packs.$curation: Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack --spec): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, desert pinned, brief forced, certified in calm air AND under the authored wind, and DEFENDED both ways. Certification rates: pocket par 2 42/48, island par 1 48/48, ridge par 1 2/48, pocket par 2 43/48, island par 1 48/48, pocket par 3 36/48, island par 2 48/48, pocket par 1 43/48, pocket par 3 38/48, island par 2 48/48. NO BEND AND NO BOMBER, and both are the ground's answer rather than a preference. Scouting desert at demand 1.15 and again at 1.00 returned bend 0/32 at every par with all 32 rejections failing STORY FIT rather than defence — desert does not draw doglegs at all, which is a different fact from pack 4 and pack 7's no-bomber finding and is worth keeping separate. Bomber was 0/32 at every par, all undefended, the same shape city and arctic gave. Demand was not the binding constraint: the two scouts were identical. That leaves pocket, island and a single ridge par, which is why this pack is five collars, four moats and one berm. TWO HOLES WERE RE-SWEPT A RUNG LOWER. Hole 2 was authored par 2 and hole 10 par 3; at those pars the ideal player beat par in calm air AND under the authored wind, so par could not be missed by anybody. Holes 6 and 7 carry the same warning and were KEPT, because their ideal only beats par in calm and the authored wind restores it — that is the line this run drew, and it is a judgement rather than a gate. No gate was softened. Sweep date: 2026-08-15.
packs.$tuning: THE STRENGTH MOVES AND THE BEARING DOES NOT, and that is the pack. Mean change in wind strength between consecutive holes is 9.1 mph, against 2.4–4.7 for every pack shipped before it — roughly double the loosest of them. Mean change in bearing is 17 degrees, which sits with pack 7 (14) and pack 3 (24) at the tight end and nowhere near pack 1 (93) or pack 2 (146). That inversion is the whole point and it is the answer to a note left on the season proposal: a moving BEARING is not novel, because packs 1, 2, 5 and 6 already swing it 176–180 degrees across ten holes. A moving STRENGTH is, and holding the bearing still is what makes it legible — with both moving, nothing tells the player which one cost them the hole. It also agrees with the ground: desert defends with collars and moats, both of them radius defences that a mis-carried throw fails, and carry is exactly what a strength change breaks. STAR LINES ARE COMPUTED, NOT MEASURED. packPar 18, so elite = 18 - 4 = 14 and target = 14 + 5 = 19, straight off LevelStarLines. The harness's totals were deliberately not consulted: its ideal player takes two strokes on nearly every hole whatever the par, so its pack totals sit in one 20–25 band for the whole trail and run backwards against real play. Reading them is what gave a par-16 pack a 3-star line of 22 before the 2026-08-15 retune. ONE GALE, on the long hole (9, at 135m), per the arc's rule. MEDIUM IS THE FLOOR: five medium, four hard, one gale, nothing calmer. Ten holes, front five and back five, packPar 18.

Certification rates: pocket par 2 48/48, bend par 2 28/48, island par 2 48/48, ridge par 2 42/48, bend par 2 29/48, pocket par 2 48/48, island par 2 48/48, ridge par 2 46/48, bomber par 3 30/48, bend par 3 32/48. JUNGLE IS THE FIRST TRAIL SCENERY THAT DEFENDS EVERY BRIEF: bend, ridge, pocket, bomber and island all certify here at every par (scout at demand 1.15: bend 18-21/32, bomber 19-24/32 with the rejections split between story fit and undefended rather than all undefended), which is the opposite of desert (no bend, no bomber), city and arctic (no bomber). THREE HOLES WERE RE-SWEPT A RUNG HIGHER. Holes 1, 3 and 8 were authored par 1 and the top-ranked candidate on each took the ideal player THREE strokes in calm air -- not a hole that could be missed by anybody, a hole that could not be made by anybody. Raising them to par 2 is the honest label for this ground, and the same spec swept on volcano and park gave the same ideal totals (31 and 32 against jungle's 34), so this is the ranking finding the most defended hole on dense ground rather than a jungle quirk. Demand made no difference: 1.15 and 1.35 chose byte-identical winners. No gate was softened. Sweep date: 2026-09-06.
packs.$tuning: THE IDEAL PLAYER NEEDS 34 STROKES FOR A PAR-22 PACK, against 22 for a par-19 p7 and 19 for a par-18 p8, and that gap is the pack. Every shipped pack before it sits between +0 and +8 over its par for the perfect player; this one is +12, because every candidate the ranking prefers is buried in cover (8-15 props behind the pin, 7-15 guarding) and the ideal has to route round it. The star lines are computed from par as LevelStarLines requires (elite 18, target 23) and NOT from the harness, which means 2 stars here is a perfect player's score minus eleven. That is the trail getting harder at its ninth stop, on purpose, and it is also the first thing a reviewer should decide whether they believe. Wind is a crosswind the whole way, alternating sides hole to hole (88/272/95/268/100/262/84/278/92/265), so every tee is an aim-off read and none is a loft read; the strength is medium on the even holes and hard on the odd, with the one gale on the 153m bomber. Four greens carry a wet approach (holes 1, 3, 5, 7), which is the "held back is wet" half of the mechanic.

Certification rates: pocket par 1 48/48, bomber par 2 12/48, ridge par 1 39/48, bomber par 2 19/48, bend par 2 19/48, bomber par 3 13/48, island par 1 48/48, ridge par 2 26/48, bomber par 3 21/48, bend par 2 17/48. Every bomber winner reports 0 guarding, which is what a bomber is -- the defence is the carry, and the sweep certifies them as defended on the water and cover behind the pin, not on a collar. Hole 8's fourth runner-up carried an IDEAL BEATS PAR warning and was not chosen; the winner does not. Holes 1 and 7 have runners-up the ideal plays a stroke better than the winner; the ranking preferred the more defended hole and this run kept the ranking, as the settled rule says. Space was scouted for this slot and found as narrow as desert -- pocket and island only, bend 3-9/32 failing story fit, ridge 1-7/32 and bomber 0-1/32 all undefended -- and is recorded here so the next run does not rediscover it. packs.$tuning: DISTANCE IS THE DEFENCE. Four bombers at 136, 136, 144 and 168m, and the ideal player takes 3 on every one of them in calm air whatever the par, so the two par-2 bombers (holes 2 and 4) are the holes that cost this pack its stars: par is a rung the perfect player does not reach. That is deliberate and it is the same shape as p5's hole 8 (ideal 5 on par 3), the last time reef was dealt. Ideal total 27 against packPar 19, a +8 gap, which sits with p1 and p5 and well under p9's +12 -- the trail steps up at nine and eases at ten rather than climbing twice. Star lines are computed (elite 15, target 20), not read off the harness. Wind bearings are quartering (10/140/40/215/320/150/45/230/130/310) rather than the pure crosswinds of p9, so half the reads are partly a loft read, and the gale is on the 168m hole 9 where it is the whole hole.
